newsitem.title: UK: Andersen awaits judgement on a UK De Lorean trial.
newsitem.headline: Andersen awaits judgement on a UK De Lorean trial.

text.p: The British High Court has completed its hearing into Arthur Andersen's application to have reopened the government's lawsuit against the firm that dealt with its auditing activities for the bankrupt De Lorean car firm.
"We look forward to learning Justice Colman's judgement," Arthur Andersen said in a statement on Thursday.
The accounting firm also said the counsel for the government confirmed during the hearing that the embargo against Arther Andersen undertaking government work had been "substantially relaxed".
This will allow Arthur Andersen to tender for government work for the first time in 12 years. However, no staff involved in the De Lorean audit will be allowed to participate.

"We were gratified that the government has relaxed these restrictions. We now hope that the case will come to trial in the UK as quickly as possible as it is so long since the events in question took place, the firm said.
Suits were filed against Arthur Andersen by Britain's Department of Economic Development and the trustee for De Lorean Motor Cars Ltd.

In 1985, the then-government served a writ on Arthur Andersen who were auditors to De Lorean which collapsed in 1982 with the loss of 2,000 jobs in Northern Ireland and nearly 80 million pounds ($134.8 million) in public funds.
The hearing began in the UK courts but was then taken to the Federal Court in New York which dismissed the case in February 1997.

At issue is whether the government agency made a new investment decision for federal securities law purposes when it agreed in 1980 to revise the terms of a put (arrangement) it held with respect to preference shares of De Lorean.
The suits arose out of an 1978 agreement by De Lorean to build sports cars in Northern Ireland.

Andersen's role was to certify the company's financial statements in the agreement by the British government agency to invest 17.8 million pounds into the project and to extend 44.9 million pounds more in grants, loans and loan guarantees. But De Lorean collapsed and later sought bankruptcy-law protection. ($ = 0.593 British Pounds)
